pull.title: ipc: hold event loop references when using it in `CapnpProtocol`
pull.body:
`EventLoop::loop()` exits when its reference count reaches zero. In `serve()` mode, the parent connection is the only reference keeping the loop running. Other `CapnpProtocol` methods called from threads not handling parent IPC requests do not hold their own references and therefore depend on the parent connection remaining alive.

Add `loopRef()` (code suggested by @ryanofsky in https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/376#discussion_r4268952676), which returns a new reference to the event loop or throws if the loop is not running or is shutting down, and use it in the methods that need the loop. Protect `m_loop` with a new `m_loop_mutex` to prevent `serve()` from destroying the loop while `loopRef()` is accessing it.

events.body: Code review 2d001df8a60a82c286ca46b04de2917be4a5c74f. Thanks for picking this up! The approach looks right, but the `loopRef()` code I suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/376#discussion_r4268952676 has a bug: it can call `EventLoop::done()` after the loop has stopped, which reads an unset optional (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36572#discussion_r4568542751). Rather than patching that check, I think it is simpler to drop it: if `serve()` holds an owner reference like `startLoop()` does and releases it when the parent disconnects, `loopRef()` can just add a reference, and `setup_ref` and the try/catch in `disconnectIncoming()` go away. I'd ACK with that or another fix.
